key_insight: Self-supervised pretraining can turn neutrino detector data into a reusable foundation-style model, improving performance even when labeled data is limited. The approach helps deep learning systems better classify events, reconstruct measurements, and transfer knowledge across different detector technologies.
problem_solved: Neutrino detectors produce highly complex, heterogeneous data, and expert labels are expensive and scarce. This paper addresses the challenge of building AI models that can learn effectively from large unlabeled datasets and generalize across different detector types.
method: Pretrain neural networks with self-supervised learning on large collections of detector events without requiring labels.
Fine-tune the pretrained models on downstream tasks such as event classification and reconstruction.
Test transferability across heterogeneous neutrino detector technologies to evaluate robustness and reuse.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how foundation-model ideas can be adapted to scientific instrumentation where labels are scarce and data are diverse. It points to a more data-efficient and transferable workflow for building models in complex experimental domains.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing unlabeled pretraining followed by task-specific fine-tuning

Icon set for classification, reconstruction, and data efficiency improvements
paper_title: Towards foundation-style models for energy-frontier heterogeneous neutrino detectors via self-supervised pretraining
paper_authors: Saúl Alonso-Monsalve, Fabio Cufino, Umut Kose, Anna Mascellani, André Rubbia
